programs.name: Humanity AI
programs.amount_note: Five-year collective commitment announced Oct 14, 2025. It combines aligned grantmaking by each funder with a pooled fund. The first pooled grants (May 12, 2026) were more than $18M: $8M to inaugural grantees, $3M for AI Civics and a planned $10M open call.
funders: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
programs.manager: Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors (fiscal sponsor; manages pooled fund)
programs.description: A ten-foundation coalition funding a people-centered future for AI, covering democracy, education, culture and the arts, work and the economy, and security. Partners began aligned grantmaking in fall 2025, and the pooled fund began making grants in 2026.

programs.name: Artists Make Technology (AMT)
programs.amount_note: $6.5M committed by four funders as of Jan 7, 2026, toward an $11M three-year goal: AMT Lab $6M, AMT Pathways $4M and AMT Assemblies $1M.
programs.description: An arts-and-technology initiative anchored by DDF and Mozilla. Its AMT Lab, the second iteration of DDF's Performing Arts Technologies Lab, funds performing artists working with technology. The first cohort of 20 projects (from 392 applications) was announced Oct 28, 2026 at MozFest in Barcelona. The first cohort of 20 grantees (announced Oct 28, 2026) was described as spanning the U.S.

programs.name: Doris Duke Foundation and Ford Foundation grants supporting technology infrastructure in the performing arts
programs.amount_note: "More than $4 million" over five years (a minimum figure), announced July 6, 2026. The page does not give each funder's share.
programs.description: Grants made in partnership with Ford for performing-arts technology infrastructure, several focused on disability arts and access. Grantees include Kinetic Light (multisensory access technology), Open Circle Theatre (VitaNova), Junebug Productions, New York Live Arts' Healing Project, Producer Hub, and SOZO Impact & Relaxed Animals (EARTH.SPEAKS with the Osage Nation).

programs.name: Artist Relief
programs.amount_note: Cumulative raised. The fund launched Apr 8, 2020 as a $10M campaign: a $5M Mellon seed gift matched by about $5M from 20+ funders. DDF's own grant was $500,000 (Apr 13, 2020).
funders: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts
John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
programs.manager: Coalition of Academy of American Poets, Artadia, Creative Capital, Foundation for Contemporary Arts, MAP Fund, National YoungArts Foundation, United States Artists
programs.description: An emergency COVID-19 fund that gave $5,000 unrestricted grants to 4,682 artists and writers across 13 funding cycles. The funder list here is partial; the fund names 24 initial matching funders plus 2021 matchers.

programs.name: NYC COVID-19 Response & Impact Fund
programs.amount_note: Initial commitment from 18 founding funders at launch (Mar 20, 2020). By mid-2020 the fund had issued more than $110M in grants and interest-free loans. DDF's share is not disclosed.
funders: Joan Ganz Cooney & Holly Peterson Fund
programs.manager: New York Community Trust (grants); Nonprofit Finance Fund (loans)
programs.description: A pooled emergency fund giving grants and interest-free loans to New York City social-services and arts and culture nonprofits hit by COVID-19. More than 768 nonprofits were supported.

programs.name: COVID-19 Arts Aid PHL Fund
programs.amount_note: Amount awarded by June 2020 to 467 organizations and 1,025 artists. William Penn Foundation gave a $2.5M lead grant. DDF's share is not disclosed.
funders: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
programs.description: A regional emergency relief fund for Greater Philadelphia arts and culture organizations and individual artists during COVID-19. DDF was named a partner at launch.

programs.name: Coronavirus Dance Relief Fund
programs.amount_note: Total awarded March–September 2020. DDF's share is not disclosed.
programs.description: Dance/NYC's COVID-19 relief fund for New York City freelance dance workers and dance-making organizations. Funder lists vary by round, so this list is partial.

programs.name: COVID-19 Fund to Retain Clinical Scientists
programs.amount_note: Total awarded in Nov 2021 to 22 U.S. medical schools (about $500K–$550K each over 2 years). The June 2021 call offered up to $10M. Individual funders paid for specific schools' grants; for example, AHA funded Duke's.
programs.description: Institutional grants to U.S. medical schools to support early-career physician-scientists whose family caregiving duties grew during COVID-19. It builds on DDCF's earlier single-funder Fund to Retain Clinical Scientists.

programs.name: Collective to Strengthen Pathways for Health Research
programs.amount_note: No amount disclosed. The collective held 18 symposia in 2025. In 2026 it opened a one-time collaborative funding call, "Demonstrating Health Solutions Science in Action" (pre-proposals due Nov 18, 2026), with intake centralized at DDF.
programs.description: A DDF-led funder collective to raise attention and resources for "health solutions science": research on disease prevention, care delivery and clinical encounters, as opposed to basic biomedical science. Dana described it as newly launched in Sept 2024.

programs.name: Opportunities for Prevention and Transformation Initiative (OPT-In for Families)
programs.amount_note: Three-year initiative total: about $9M per site from a coalition of funders. Individual funder shares are not disclosed.
programs.manager: Foster America (overall coordination); partners Harvard Kennedy School Government Performance Lab, Chapin Hall, Think of Us
programs.description: A demonstration initiative to shift child welfare toward prevention through community response pathways. Its four sites are Washington, D.C., Kentucky, Oregon and South Carolina.

programs.name: Institutional Challenge Grant
programs.amount_note: About $2.6M per annual cohort (2023, 2025 and 2026 rounds), or $650K per grantee over 3 years. The year is DDF's earliest confirmed co-funding round; it may have started earlier.
programs.description: Grants to university–public agency/nonprofit research-practice partnerships working to reduce inequality in youth outcomes. Bezos joined in 2023 and Annie E. Casey in 2026; AIR co-funded the 2021 round. Some funded projects concern youth leaving foster care and child welfare.

programs.name: Tribal Nations Conservation Pledge
programs.amount_note: Total commitments from 15 funders over five years, announced March 2023. DDF's share was about $32M (roughly one third). Each funder directs its own grants, and funders can also give directly to the fund.
programs.manager: Native Americans in Philanthropy and Biodiversity Funders Group (organizers; Tribal Nations Funding Collaborative)
programs.description: A funder pledge, tied to the America the Beautiful Challenge, directing money to conservation led by Tribes, inter-Tribal organizations and Indigenous-led nonprofits. Only 5 of the 15 funders are named in the sources.

programs.name: NEFA National Dance Project
programs.amount_note: No amounts disclosed. DDF has been a lead funder since 1999, alongside Mellon. Mellon ended its NDP support in 2025. The final Production Grant cohort was named in Sept 2026; Presentation grants and the Travel Fund continue.
funders: Aliad Fund at the Boston Foundation
programs.manager: New England Foundation for the Arts (NEFA)
programs.description: A long-running national regranting program supporting the creation and U.S. touring of dance works. It falls within the 2018–2026 window as an active co-funded program.

programs.name: NEFA National Theater Project
programs.amount_note: DDCF's 2-year grant (Dec 2017) expanding Creation and Touring grants. Mellon is the lead funder; its amount is not disclosed. NEFA said in Sept 2024 that NTP was entering its final grant cycle in its current form, so the end year is unconfirmed.
programs.manager: New England Foundation for the Arts (NEFA)
programs.description: A NEFA regranting program supporting the creation and national touring of devised theater, with lead funding from Mellon and additional support from DDF.

programs.name: Ethiopia Data Use Partnership (DUP)
programs.amount_note: DDCF grant of $5M over 5 years (awarded Jan 1, 2018) to strengthen Ethiopia's health information system in four regions. Gates' larger primary funding (awarded Oct 2016) is not included. The end year is the nominal end of DDCF's 5-year grant.
programs.description: A partnership with Ethiopia's Ministry of Health and regional health bureaus to improve health data quality and use, part of the Phase 2 work of DDCF's African Health Initiative. The DUP site says it is "Funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the Doris Duke Charitable Foundation".

excluded.name: Doris Duke Performing Artist Recovery Fund (2021, $3M)
excluded.reason: DDCF-only money. NYCT administered it through a fund DDCF created at NYCT and did not co-fund.

excluded.name: WCS Climate Adaptation Fund
excluded.reason: Funded by DDCF alone and managed by WCS. No co-funders found; its collaboration with the Climate Resilience Fund was a report, not funding.

excluded.name: Performing Arts Readiness (LYRASIS)
excluded.reason: Every grant found was from Mellon. No evidence of DDF funding.

excluded.name: Building Bridges co-funding (Sundance Building Bridges Fellowship, CAAM Documentary Fund)
excluded.reason: Sundance, the Islamic Scholarship Fund and CAAM are DDF grantees or administrators, not co-funders. No pooled or co-funded Building Bridges fund was found.

excluded.name: Clinical Scientist Development Award (CSDA)
excluded.reason: No partner co-funders found on DDF's CSDA announcements (2020–2023).

excluded.name: African Health Initiative (overall, 2007–2024)
excluded.reason: Launched in 2007 as a DDCF-funded $100M initiative, before the study window. Only its Ethiopia DUP component has a documented co-funder (Gates), so that component is listed separately.

excluded.name: Adaptation and Resilience Fund (Rockefeller Foundation, ClimateWorks; 2025)
excluded.reason: DDF is not among the listed funders.

excluded.name: Disability Futures Fellows (Ford and Mellon) / Ford Disability x Tech Fund (Borealis)
Forum on Climate Investing with RockCreek (2023)
excluded.reason: A convening at Duke Farms, not a funding program.

excluded.name: Gates/Wellcome global health, malaria or tropical disease co-funding (2018–2026)
excluded.reason: Searches found no such DDF program apart from the Ethiopia DUP.

leads.lead: Biodiversity funder collaborative (Consultative Group on Biological Diversity)
leads.note: DDF made a $250K, 1-year grant (Nov 2024) to develop a new collaborative philanthropic effort to reverse U.S. biodiversity loss. No name, pooled structure or co-funders were confirmed. Source: https://www.dorisduke.org/grants/what-weve-funded/Grant-Recipients/consultative-group-on-biological-diversity6
DDF gave $750K to launch a platform hosting revolving loan funds for conservation organizations and funders. It may be a multi-funder vehicle; co-funders were not verified.

leads.lead: Ethiopia DUP and the Global Fund
leads.note: One search summary said a DDF page lists the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria as a DUP co-funder. The page could not be confirmed, and JSI's site names only Gates and DDCF.
The sources do not state whether AMT Lab or Pathways grantees must be U.S.-based. The 2026 cohort was announced in Barcelona. Check the 2026 cohort page (Mozilla returned 403).

leads.lead: Humanity AI open call and grantee geography
leads.note: A $10M open call was planned for summer 2026. Grantee countries are not stated; the Pulitzer Center grant supports journalists worldwide.

leads.lead: Child welfare award co-funded by Casey, Doris Duke and Aviv
leads.note: An Inside Philanthropy piece (May 22, 2024, 'Seven funders working to improve child welfare and foster care') says Casey, Doris Duke and Aviv contributed to an unnamed award. Not identified.
A W.T. Grant PDF of 2018–2020 awards reportedly lists a project jointly supported by DDCF, so DDF's co-funding may predate 2021.

leads.lead: DDCF pandemic statement on 'numerous collaborative pooled funds'
leads.note: In 2020 DDCF said it joined numerous pooled COVID relief funds nationwide. Others beyond NYC, Arts Aid PHL, Dance/NYC and Artist Relief probably exist, such as regional arts or jazz relief funds.

leads.lead: Original Fund to Retain Clinical Scientists (2015–)
leads.note: Duke's FRCS materials say it is supported by AHA and DDCF ('AHA-DDCF', 2023), which suggests AHA co-funding of the non-COVID FRCS after 2021. Not verified.
The press-release PDF returned 404, so co-funders were not verified.

leads.lead: Shangri La / Islamic arts international programs
leads.note: Not researched for co-funding; a possible source of international activity.
